Time Series Analysis

From ARMA to the Kalman Filter

Dynamic regression · ARMA · Volatility · Unit roots · Forecasting · Cointegration · VAR/SVAR · External instruments · Local projections · State space
slides.title: Time Series Analysis

slides.html:
Four Questions to Keep Apart

  1. Forecasting: does the past improve predictions of the future?
  2. Dynamic propagation: how does a shock's effect unfold over horizons?
  3. Causal identification: is the shock exogenous and economically meaningful?
  4. State estimation: how do we update beliefs about an unobserved state?

A good fit or forecast ≠ causal identification; the Kalman filter ≠ a fix for endogeneity.
slides.title: Four Questions to Keep Apart

slides.html: 1–3. Dynamic Regression and OLS
slides.title: 1–3. Dynamic Regression and OLS

slides.html:
Distributed Lags and Long-Run Multipliers

y_t=\alpha+\sum_{j=0}^{q}\delta_jx_{t-j}+u_t
  • one-period +1: response at h is \delta_h
  • permanent +1: cumulative \sum_{j\le h}\delta_j, long run \theta=\sum\delta_j
  • reparametrise with \delta_j(x_{t-j}-x_t) ⟹ the coefficient on x_t is \theta, with its standard error
  • with \phi y_{t-1}: long-run effect \sum\delta_j/(1-\phi)
slides.title: Distributed Lags and Long-Run Multipliers

slides.html:
Strict vs Contemporaneous Exogeneity

  • Strict: E(u_t\mid X)=0 ⟹ finite-sample unbiasedness, exact t/F
  • Contemporaneous: E(u_t\mid x_t)=0 ⟹ consistency and asymptotic normality only
  • models with y_{t-1}: strict exogeneity necessarily fails
\sqrt T(\hat\beta-\beta)\Rightarrow N(0,Q^{-1}SQ^{-1}),\quad S=\text{long-run covariance of the score }x_tu_t

Needs stationarity + weak dependence for LLN/CLT.
slides.title: Strict vs Contemporaneous Exogeneity

slides.html: 4–5. ARMA and Box–Jenkins
slides.title: 4–5. ARMA and Box–Jenkins

slides.html:
MA(1) and Invertibility

y_t=\mu+\varepsilon_t+\theta\varepsilon_{t-1}
  • \gamma_0=(1+\theta^2)\sigma^2, \rho_1=\dfrac{\theta}{1+\theta^2}, \rho_{k>1}=0
  • any finite MA is stationary; invertible (|\theta|<1) lets us recover innovations from data
  • \theta and 1/\theta share an ACF ⟹ choose the invertible one
slides.title: MA(1) and Invertibility

slides.html:
General ARMA

\phi(L)y_t=c+\theta(L)\varepsilon_t,\qquad y_t-\mu=\sum\psi_j\varepsilon_{t-j},\ \psi=\theta/\phi
  • stationary: AR roots outside the unit circle; invertible: MA roots outside
  • software "inverse roots" must be inside
  • \psi_h = propagation = weights of multi-step forecast errors
  • white noise: uncorrelated ≠ independent
slides.title: General ARMA

slides.html:
Information Criteria and Diagnostics

  • \mathrm{AIC}\simeq\ln\hat\sigma^2+\dfrac{2k}{T}, \mathrm{BIC}\simeq\ln\hat\sigma^2+\dfrac{k\ln T}{T} (same sample)
  • Ljung–Box: Q(m)=T(T+2)\sum\dfrac{\hat\rho_j^2}{T-j}\sim\chi^2_{m-p-q}
  • ACF of residuals and squared residuals should look white

Box–Jenkins: look at data → make stationary → ACF/PACF candidates → estimate and diagnose → compare IC → out-of-sample evaluation
slides.title: Information Criteria and Diagnostics

slides.html: 6–7. Autocorrelation and Volatility
slides.title: 6–7. Autocorrelation and Volatility

slides.html:
Residual Autocorrelation

  • autocorrelated errors + strict exogeneity: OLS stays unbiased but standard errors and efficiency fail
  • with y_{t-1}: y_{t-1} correlated with u_t ⟹ OLS inconsistent, HAC cannot help
  • tests: Durbin–Watson (\approx2(1-\hat\rho), invalid with lagged dependent variables), Breusch–Godfrey LM
  • remedy: y_t=\beta_0(1-\rho)+\rho y_{t-1}+\beta_1x_t-\rho\beta_1x_{t-1}+\varepsilon_t (nonlinear constraint)
slides.title: Residual Autocorrelation

slides.html:
HAC / Newey–West

\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\beta)=\tfrac1TQ^{-1}\hat SQ^{-1},\quad\hat S=\hat\Gamma_0+\sum_{j=1}^b w_j(\hat\Gamma_j+\hat\Gamma_j'),\ w_j=1-\tfrac{j}{b+1}
Case Action
exogenous target, dependent errors HAC
omission ⟹ endogeneity fix model / IV; HAC useless

Bandwidth b ≠ AR order; HAC does not change point estimates.
slides.title: HAC / Newey–West

slides.html:
Case: NYSE Daily Returns

Model Point AIC
ARCH(5) squared residuals still correlated -6.8215
GARCH(1,1) \hat\alpha=0.067,\ \hat\beta=0.920 -6.8680
  • \hat\alpha+\hat\beta=0.987: very persistent volatility
  • mean hard to predict, volatility easy to predict
slides.title: Case: NYSE Daily Returns

slides.html: 8–9. Unit Roots and Forecasting
slides.title: 8–9. Unit Roots and Forecasting

slides.html:
Trend Stationary vs Random Walk

trend stationary random walk
treatment detrend difference
shock dies out permanent
IRF \to0 \equiv1
variance constant t\sigma^2

A random walk with constant mean is still non-stationary.
slides.title: Trend Stationary vs Random Walk

slides.html:
Reading an ADF Result

  • example: \hat\gamma=-0.08, se =0.03 ⟹ \tau=-2.67>-2.86: fail to reject
  • using -1.645 would wrongly reject
  • too few lags: size distortion; too many: low power
  • failing to reject ≠ proving a unit root (short samples, breaks)
  • report: levels/logs, deterministics, lags, sample, statistic
slides.title: Reading an ADF Result

slides.html:
Case: US Inflation Persistence

  • 1960–2010, 204 quarters of CPI inflation
  • ADF (intercept, 2 lags) -3.078; 4 lags -2.76: conclusion depends on lags
  • we assume a highly persistent I(0) and proceed
  • sparse AR(6) (lags 1,2,3,6) slightly better on AIC; BIC picks AR(3)
slides.title: Case: US Inflation Persistence

slides.html:
By Hand, and Evaluation

  • AR(1): \mu=10,\phi=0.8,\sigma=2,y_T=15 ⟹ forecasts 14, 13.2; two-step variance 6.56; interval [8.18,18.22]
  • the interval is pointwise, not a joint band for the path
  • evaluate with same origins, same horizon, out of sample; DM =\bar d/\sqrt{\hat S_d/N} (long-run variance)
  • back-transforming logs: mean \exp(m+v/2), median \exp(m)
slides.title: By Hand, and Evaluation

slides.html: 10. Cointegration
slides.title: 10. Cointegration

slides.html:
Testing for Cointegration

  • Given by theory: construct and test directly (e.g. spread r_6-r_3)
  • Engle–Granger: levels regression → unit-root test on residuals with special critical values (two variables, intercept, 5%: -3.34)
  • super-consistency (rate T) ≠ ordinary t is valid
slides.title: Testing for Cointegration

slides.html:
Stock–Watson: Two Econometricians

first second
specification levels spurious regression + trend long-run relation + lagged dynamics
findings price significant, trend significant long-run coefficient \approx0.94, price has no predictive power
issue stochastic trend read as deterministic; wrong unit-root distribution closer to the true mechanism
slides.title: Stock–Watson: Two Econometricians

slides.html:
Error Correction

\Delta y_t=\lambda(y_{t-1}-a-\beta x_{t-1})+\delta_0\Delta x_t+u_t,\quad\lambda=\phi-1
  • derived from an ARDL(1,1): \beta=\dfrac{\delta_0+\delta_1}{1-\phi}\ne\delta_0
  • modelling only differences discards "how far off we are"
  • VECM: \Delta Y_t=\Pi Y_{t-1}+\sum\Gamma_i\Delta Y_{t-i}+u_t, \Pi=\alpha\beta'
  • r cointegrating relations ⟹ n-r common trends
slides.title: Error Correction

slides.html: 11–13. VARs and Structural Identification
slides.title: 11–13. VARs and Structural Identification

slides.html:
Reduced-Form VAR

Y_t=c+A_1Y_{t-1}+\dots+A_pY_{t-p}+u_t,\qquad E(u_tu_t')=\Sigma_u
  • equation-by-equation OLS; parameter count n(1+np)+n(n+1)/2
  • companion form: Z_t=\mathcal AZ_{t-1}+v_t; stable ⟺ eigenvalues inside the unit circle
  • Y_t=\mu+\sum\Psi_hu_{t-h}, VAR(1): \Psi_h=A_1^h
  • Granger predictability ≠ structural causality
slides.title: Reduced-Form VAR

slides.html:
Why Identification Is Needed

u_t=B^{-1}\varepsilon_t=C\epsilon_t,\qquad\Sigma_u=CC'
  • \Sigma_u: n(n+1)/2 numbers; C: n^2 unknowns
  • need n(n-1)/2 more restrictions
  • any orthogonal Q: (CQ)(CQ)'=CC'

One innovation covariance is compatible with infinitely many "structural shocks".
slides.title: Why Identification Is Needed

slides.html:
IRFs, Cumulative Responses and FEVD

  • units: one unit / one s.d. / 25 bp are not directly comparable
  • cumulative response \sum_{h\le H}\Theta_{ij,h}: growth rate → log level
  • FEVD: \dfrac{\sum_h\Theta_{ij,h}^2}{\sum_k\sum_h\Theta_{ik,h}^2}, depends on identification
  • bands: delta method / bootstrap; pointwise ≠ joint
slides.title: IRFs, Cumulative Responses and FEVD

slides.html:
Case: Kilian's Oil Shocks

Z_t=(\Delta prod,\ rea,\ rpo), 24 lags, recursive identification:

Shock Oil-price response
supply disruption small, temporary
global demand delayed, persistent
oil-specific demand immediate, large, persistent

The same price rise, different shocks behind it, different macro effects.
slides.title: Case: Kilian's Oil Shocks

slides.html:
Long-Run Variance ≠ Ordinary Variance

  • AR(1): \operatorname{Var}(x_t)=\dfrac{\sigma^2}{1-\phi^2}, \Lambda=\dfrac{\sigma^2}{(1-\phi)^2}
  • \phi=0.5: 4/3 vs 4
  • limits: sensitive to low frequencies, lag order, near-unit roots, breaks
  • long-run restrictions are not "more causal" than short-run ones
slides.title: Long-Run Variance ≠ Ordinary Variance

slides.html: 14–16. External Shocks, LP and Monetary Policy
slides.title: 14–16. External Shocks, LP and Monetary Policy

slides.html:
Identifying from Outside the System

Method Information Risk
short-run zeros internal timing ordering assumption
long-run zeros economic theory low frequency
narrative / high-frequency records, announcement windows expectations, information effects
external IV proxy for the shock weak instruments, contamination

Policy changes are mostly reactions; we need variation "outside the rule".
slides.title: Identifying from Outside the System

slides.html:
High-Frequency Surprises

\Delta r=\Delta r^{exp}+\Delta r^{surprise},\qquad\Delta r^{surprise}\approx\frac{m}{m-d}(f_d-f_{d-1})
  • the expected part is already in prices
  • event study: R_t=\beta_0+\beta_1\Delta r^{surp}+e_t, full-sample \hat\beta_1=-3.87
  • subsamples: -4.45,\ -0.98,\ +0.16,\ -7.76 ⟹ parameters may be time-varying
slides.title: High-Frequency Surprises

slides.html:
Proxy SVAR

Conditions: E(z\epsilon_1)\ne0, E(z\epsilon_j)=0 ⟹ E(u_tz_t)\propto C_{\cdot1}

  • normalise: b=q/q_1; \Psi_hb = response to "policy variable +1 unit on impact"
  • example: covariances 0.02 and -0.06 ⟹ relative response -3; 25 bp ⟹ -0.75
  • noisy proxy: direct regression attenuates by \dfrac{\sigma_\epsilon^2}{\sigma_\epsilon^2+\sigma_\nu^2}; as an IV it does not
  • check: relevance, exclusion, window contamination, cross-period exclusion
slides.title: Proxy SVAR

slides.html:
LP-IV and Asymmetry

  • LP-IV: \theta_h=\dfrac{E(\tilde z\,\tilde y_{t+h})}{E(\tilde z\,\tilde x)} — the denominator cannot be dropped
  • the response includes instrument-induced later policy, not "change now only"
  • asymmetry: must nest the linear benchmark y=\alpha+\beta x+\delta x^+ +u and test \delta=0
  • state dependence: define the state with pre-shock information; interactions need interacted instruments
  • variances of cumulative responses need covariances
slides.title: LP-IV and Asymmetry

slides.html:
Monetary Policy: Six Methods

Method Identification / response
1 CEE SVAR block recursive + VAR
2 R&R hybrid VAR R&R residual + short-run restrictions
3 R&R + LP horizon-by-horizon regressions
4 R&R Proxy SVAR R&R as instrument
5 High-freq Proxy SVAR futures surprise as instrument
6 High-freq + LP horizon-by-horizon regressions
slides.title: Monetary Policy: Six Methods

slides.html:
Lessons from the Comparison

  • the same question, different method / sample / controls ⟹ different answers (price puzzle, expansion vs contraction)
  • identifying information × propagation estimator (VAR or LP) are two dimensions
  • contemporaneous controls in an LP may imply recursive restrictions
  • for an "anomalous" response: check sign and normalisation, definitions, sample, information set, controls, instrument contamination
  • the literature is not consistent in summarising method 6
slides.title: Lessons from the Comparison

slides.html: 17–19. Likelihood, Kalman Filter and TVP
slides.title: 17–19. Likelihood, Kalman Filter and TVP

slides.html:
Prediction-Error Decomposition

\ell(\vartheta)=-\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\Big[\ln2\pi+\ln f_t+\frac{\eta_t^2}{f_t}\Big]
  • chain rule: L=p(y_1)\prod p(y_t\mid y_{1:t-1})
  • \Omega=ADA', \eta=A^{-1}(Y-\mu): \eta_t innovation, f_t its variance
  • the likelihood is a density, not a probability of the parameter
  • constraints: e^\psi, logistic, GARCH normalisation; delta method
slides.title: Prediction-Error Decomposition

slides.html:
State Space

y_t=H_t\beta_t+e_t,\ e_t\sim N(0,R)\qquad\beta_t=d+F\beta_{t-1}+v_t,\ v_t\sim N(0,Q)
Model Form
fixed-coefficient regression F=I,\ Q=0
time-varying regression H_t=x_t', random walk
local linear trend level + slope

Initialisation: stationary → unconditional variance; random walk → diffuse prior.
slides.title: State Space

slides.html:
The Kalman Recursion

Predict \beta_{t|t-1}=d+F\beta_{t-1|t-1} P_{t|t-1}=FPF'+Q

Innovation \eta_t=y_t-H\beta_{t|t-1}, S_t=HP_{t|t-1}H'+R

Update K_t=P_{t|t-1}H'S_t^{-1} \beta_{t|t}=\beta_{t|t-1}+K_t\eta_t P_{t|t}=P_{t|t-1}-K_tHP_{t|t-1}

Follows directly from the conditional distribution of a joint normal; the Joseph form keeps positive semi-definiteness.
slides.title: The Kalman Recursion

slides.html:
Kalman Inside MLE

  1. fix hyperparameters and initial conditions
  2. filter t=1..T to get \eta_t,S_t
  3. accumulate \ell_t=-\tfrac12[m\ln2\pi+\ln|S_t|+\eta_t'S_t^{-1}\eta_t]
  4. the optimiser changes hyperparameters; repeat until convergence
  5. rerun at the final hyperparameters to output the state path

Missing observation: predict only, no update; do not fill with 0.
slides.title: Kalman Inside MLE

slides.html:
Nonlinearity: Linearisation

J_t=\big(1-\bar\lambda,\ (1-\bar\lambda)\pi^f,\ (1-\bar\lambda)g^f,\ \bar\lambda(1-\bar\lambda)(r_{t-1}-\bar m)\big)
  • y^{lin}=r-f(\bar\beta)+J\bar\beta\approx J\beta+e (extended Kalman)
  • error in the state: 5 dimensions; E(e^2)=\hat e^2+P^{ee} drives h_t
  • example: J=(0.5,\,1,\,-0.5,\,0.125)
  • 7 hyperparameters: \omega,\alpha,\beta and 4 state variances
slides.title: Nonlinearity: Linearisation

slides.html:
Different Uncertainties

Source Representation
state prediction / filtering P_{t\mid t-1},\ P_{t\mid t}
observation prediction S_t=HPH'+R (\ne R)
hyperparameter estimation Hessian / delta
linearisation needs diagnostics

\hat b\pm1.96\sqrt{P} is only a state band conditional on hyperparameters and approximations.
slides.title: Different Uncertainties

slides.title: 20. Review

slides.html:
Pick a Route by Goal

  • forecast one series: transform → stationarity → ARMA → volatility → out of sample
  • long-run relation: integration orders → cointegration → error correction
  • exogenous shock: define the shock → internal restrictions / external instruments → VAR or LP
  • time-varying coefficients: separate state and noise → likelihood + filter → check initialisation
slides.title: Pick a Route by Goal

slides.html:
Concepts Most Often Confused

Confused Distinction
stationary vs independent white noise need not be independent
HAC vs fixing endogeneity HAC only adjusts the covariance
fail to reject vs prove a unit root power, sample
cointegration vs structural identification long-run combination ≠ meaning of shocks
innovations vs structural shocks innovations are mixtures
zero now vs zero forever \Theta_1\ne0
filtering vs smoothing smoothing uses the future
slides.title: Concepts Most Often Confused

slides.html:
One-Page Summary

Forecasting → ARMA / GARCH / unit roots ⟶ multivariate → cointegration / VAR ⟶ causality → SVAR / external IV / LP ⟶ states → MLE / Kalman / TVP

  • at every step ask: which of the four questions does this quantity answer?
  • empirical numbers are quoted historical results, not re-estimated
